1.explanation: Each of these files defines a component that currently deprecates the `ariaLabel` prop in favor of `aria-label` but still only lists or handles the camel-cased prop. To achieve consistency and comply with React’s WAI-ARIA guidance, they need to: 1) add `['aria-label']` to their prop types, 2) update any PropTypes or TypeScript interfaces to accept and prefer the hyphenated version, and 3) adjust internal usage so both props remain supported (falling back to `ariaLabel`) but guide consumers to use `aria-label`. These four files represent key, widely used components (structured list wrapper, dropdown listbox, combobox, and code snippet) that need this refactor to standardize aria-label support across the library.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots illustrate an inconsistency in our React components’ prop naming for accessibility labels. In the Modal component (first image), the storybook control shows and accepts the prop aria-label (kebab-case), while in the ComboBox component (second image) the prop is named ariaLabel (camelCase). This inconsistency causes confusion and fails to follow React’s recommendation to use hyphen-cased aria attributes.
